title: EXP-119 — Hello World Part 8 Phase 2: Runtime Sign-In and Item Tile Refresh
objective: Verify the existing FX_CustomerPortal sign-in and item-tile refresh behavior in the Mongoose Web Client. Establish a clean runtime baseline, enter the tutorial test Customer ID 1 into EditCustID, activate ButtonSignIn2 exactly once, and observe whether GridItems displays recognizable FX_Items records using FX_ItemsTile. Capture the before-and-after runtime states, including visible errors and prompts. Close the runtime Form cleanly without saving data, reopen it once through the ordinary supported Web Client path, and record its initial state without repeating the sign-in activation. This is a functional UI observation, not a test of database durability or internal equivalence between object2 and objects2.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, the applicable Hello World Part 8 Phase 2 tutorial section, the EXP-117 operator Outcome, narrowly relevant EXP-114 through EXP-116 Outcomes, and the session-expiry recipe.
Create or update documentation only under experiments/EXP-119-hello-world-part-8-phase-2-runtime-tile-refresh.md and evidence/EXP-119/.
Verify the existing authenticated Web Client session before any runtime action. The operator handles authentication.

Inspect the existing FX_CustomerPortal Designer configuration read-only where needed to confirm the saved User-scope identity, GridItems binding, Tile Form, FX_SignInBtn handler, and ButtonSignIn2 Primary assignment.
Open FX_CustomerPortal using the ordinary supported Web Client Form-opening path.
Record the initial runtime display, EditCustID control, ButtonSignIn2, GridItems region, and any visible tiles or empty-state indicators.
Enter the exact tutorial test value 1 into EditCustID once and verify the displayed value.
Activate ButtonSignIn2 exactly once and record the visible response, prompts, console-error count, and resulting GridItems display.
Capture a decisive screenshot identifying FX_CustomerPortal and any rendered FX_Items tiles, including available Item, Description, Cost, or picture content.
Compare visible tiles with previously documented FX_Items test records where reliable evidence exists. Do not invent expected item counts or values.
Close the runtime FX_CustomerPortal Form once without saving business data. If an unsaved-changes prompt appears, record it verbatim and choose the permitted non-saving response.
Reopen FX_CustomerPortal once through the ordinary Web Client path and record its initial state without activating ButtonSignIn2 again.
Maintain exact browser action counts, console-error baselines and changes, prompt records, screenshot inventory, worker-written-file inventory, cleanup state, and evidence limitations.

Separate execution into bounded tasks: T1 read-only preflight, T2 single runtime sign-in activation, T3 clean close/reopen observation, and T4 documentation-only final audit. Each later task requires coordinator authorization.
Use one fresh untargeted snapshot and at most one corrected visible inspection for a recoverable reference or inspection failure. Stop if the bounded recovery fails.

acceptance_checks.description: Required sources reviewed, session usability established, FX_CustomerPortal positively identified, User-scope Designer definition confirmed without mutation, and runtime baseline recorded. Evidence: readable Form identity and scope observations, baseline screenshot, and initial console-error count.

Before activation, FX_CustomerPortal is displayed with EditCustID containing exactly 1 and the intended ButtonSignIn2 identified. Initial GridItems state recorded. Evidence: pre-activation screenshot showing Form identity, input value, button, and grid region.

Exactly one ButtonSignIn2 activation occurs, with response, prompts, errors, and resulting display recorded. A positive functional outcome requires GridItems to visibly display at least one identifiable item tile after activation. Empty, erroneous, or unidentifiable results must be reported accurately rather than treated as successful refresh. Evidence: post-activation screenshot and action audit.

The displayed tiles provide sufficient visible evidence of FX_Items data and FX_ItemsTile presentation. Item, Description, Cost, or picture values are compared against trusted prior evidence where available. An unverified rendering or empty grid does not pass this check. Evidence: readable tile screenshot and concise comparison with stated limitations.

Exactly one ordinary runtime Form close and one supported reopen are recorded without a runtime Save. The reopened Form displays its initial runtime state and is left clean. Persistence of transient input or tile state is not required. Evidence: closing response or prompt, reopened Form screenshot, and zero-Save action audit.

Final audit records exact action counts, no more than one sign-in activation, screenshots, prompts, errors, file inventory, cleanup state, and repository confinement. No Designer mutation, stored-data Save, Regenerate, unload, checkout, or deployment occurred according to worker and harness evidence. Operator git review remains authoritative. Findings are classified observed or unresolved, never replay_verified.

initial_instruction: Perform EXP-119 T1 ONLY. Read the complete AGENTS.md, the approved EXP-119 brief, the applicable Hello World Part 8 Phase 2 runtime tutorial section, the EXP-117 operator Outcome, narrowly relevant prerequisite Outcomes, and the session-expiry recipe. List browser tabs before any selection. Inspect the current authenticated session and FX_CustomerPortal read-only. Confirm User scope, Form identity, the existing GridItems Tile Form FX_ItemsTile and Tile When Always, FX_SignInBtn Collection Refresh targeting secondary collection 2, and ButtonSignIn2 Primary FX_SignInBtn, using only permitted visible Designer evidence. Record the console-error baseline and the supported ordinary Web Client runtime opening path. Review available evidence for existing FX_Items test records without assuming that current runtime data is unchanged. Capture only decisive preflight screenshots, document the proof and its limitations, and write findings exclusively under the EXP-119 record and evidence directory. If authentication is unusable or any prerequisite fails, stop for operator disposition. Do not enter Customer ID 1, activate Sign In, modify any property, perform a Save, start runtime data editing, or execute the close/reopen test. Stop at the T1 boundary and report whether T2 can safely proceed.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261018-235207-sV2Q. Rationale: EXP-118.brief.json already exists, so this proposal uses the new experiment ID EXP-119 without overwriting EXP-118. EXP-115 and EXP-116 established FX_ItemsTile. EXP-117 configured GridItems to use FX_ItemsTile, set Tile When to Always, created FX_SignInBtn with Collection Refresh targeting secondary collection 2 (FX_Items), and assigned that handler to ButtonSignIn2. EXP-117 was accepted as observed with qualifications on 2026-10-19, but runtime functionality was deliberately deferred. A single controlled runtime activation is the smallest next step. It can establish whether the configured sign-in action displays FX_Items tiles without changing the accepted Form definition or stored application data.
